tech.title: Cognition Studied How Global 1000 Engineering Teams Use Cloud Agents
tech.summary: Cognition analyzed five months of production data from Global 1000 engineering teams running Devin cloud agents and found that writing code accounted for 23% of the productive engineering hours. The other 77% came from planning, testing, security, and deployment. Learn why cost per session fell as usage grew, where enterprises point agent spend, and which use cases return the most engineering hours per session. Download the Benchmark Report >

tech.title: The Election Day Revolt That Threatens America's AI Boom
tech.summary: Recent election results show that voters are overwhelmingly against the massive build-out of compute capacity that Silicon Valley is pushing. This could rein in AI's rapid growth and become a big problem for the tech companies developing the technology, and could have effects on the wider US economy. Stalling construction could result in dire consequences for tech companies that were already struggling to secure enough compute.

tech.title: Major Investors Are Skeptical Anthropic IPO Can Achieve $1.5 Trillion Valuation
tech.summary: Major investors planning to participate in Anthropic's IPO, expected to launch the week before Thanksgiving, say the expected $1.5 trillion valuation will likely need to come down. The AI lab was expected to raise up to $100 billion, but is now predicted to raise around $80 billion, leaving it with a valuation closer to $1 trillion. Investors have revolted against AI bets this week as the midterm elections have put several AI skeptics in power, potentially slowing data center development in the US. Anthropic has avoided committing to specific plans for its IPO to maintain optionality.

tech.title: Blue Origin says it is building a higher-performing rocket engine at 1/4 the cost
tech.summary: Blue Origin has announced two significant upgrades to its New Glenn rocket that reduce the cost of manufacturing the vehicle and expand its capacity for payload delivery. The company aims to eventually launch the vehicle more than 1,000 times a year. It has started test firing a new engine that will eventually replace the BE-4 engine that powers the first stage of New Glenn. The company is also developing a hydrogen-oxygen third stage for the rocket to give it an extra kick.

tech.title: They Created a Cell That's Almost Alive. What to Do With It Now?
tech.summary: A SpudCell is an artificial cell created from lifeless ingredients that can grow, copy its DNA, divide in two, and start its cell cycle all over again. It is still far from a self-sustaining cell that any scientist could manufacture from prepared ingredients, but the technology could eventually make it easier to produce medicines, foods, and other items that could not otherwise be produced with ordinary biology. The researchers working on SpudCell hope that it will eventually be a platform for biotechnology that will allow a simple cell to be engineered in scores of useful ways. SpudCell could potentially be misused, so its researchers are taking security seriously from the start - its DNA and proteins are engineered so that it can only survive on an exotic diet of chemicals not found in nature.

tech.title: A Pile of MCP Connectors Is Not A Context Engine
tech.summary: Your agents have MCP access to Slack, Jira and GitHub. Your engineers still babysit them. Read why connectors alone fall short, and how using a real context engine can make the same coding task 83% faster and 60% cheaper. Read the blog post

tech.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
tech.summary: *sshole is a vulnerability in Linux that allows attackers to log in via SSH without knowing the password. The vulnerability exists in systems using OpenSSH with musl without pluggable authentication modules. Despite the prerequisites, the vulnerabilities likely threaten a large number of systems. It is still unclear where the vulnerability resides and what other packages may be vulnerable.

tech.title: Inside GitHub's new Git storage architecture
tech.summary: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. It can support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. The new architecture is designed to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers. This post walks through the requirements behind the design of the new architecture and explores two of its components.

tech.title: The Making of Dario Amodei
tech.summary: At the heart of Dario Amodei's worldview are two interwoven philosophies: rationalism, which aims to apply dispassionate thinking to the world, and effective altruism, which seeks to maximize social good with mathematical precision. These schools of thought form the foundation for Anthropic. As the company has grown, Amodei's views have become increasingly prominent. This article takes a look at how Anthropic's chief executive's thinking on AI was shaped.

tech.title: The Hackintosh Reborn... with AI
tech.summary: A 'Hackintosh' is a non-Apple computer running macOS. The Hackintosh community started fading away after Apple released its first ARM-based Mac and discontinued support for x86 versions of macOS. However, the rise of AI has revived activity in the space, and there has been an explosion in development, activity, and success in the past few weeks. This post lists a few recent developments, including macOS 27 running on a Snapdragon laptop, iOS 17 running on the Nintendo Switch OLED, and macOS 27.2 Beta on an ARM SBC RK3588 with Mali drivers.

tech.title: Is your documentation ready for AI agents?
tech.summary: When an agent can't use your docs, developers don't get an error. They reach for a competitor. Find out where you stand across Cursor, Claude, and ChatGPT. Score your docs.

tech.summary: This essay looks at what it takes to build a physical platform capable of performing biological experiments, measuring their outcomes reliably, and generating evidence at the scale AI requires.

tech.title: The Exploit Was the Bottleneck
tech.summary: The average time from disclosure to attack has been falling for some time, but AI has changed who can operate inside that window, and how fast known bugs get weaponized.

tech.title: I wish tech companies knew more about me
tech.summary: Tech companies track, store, and sell a lot of information - they should use it to make the user experience better.

tech.title: A database is a store for global variables
tech.summary: Two pieces of common software engineering dogma - avoid global variables and use a database for state - are partially inconsistent.

tech.title: How Musk Plans to Shake Up the US Wireless Industry
tech.summary: Elon Musk wants to combine SpaceX's Starlink satellite broadband network with mobile antennas, fiber connections, and other ground infrastructure, so that regular smartphones can seamlessly tap into signals from both Earth and space.

The model's vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements. It will be initially available through Tinker with closed weights. Full weights will be available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.

ai.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
ai.summary: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, enhancing speed, cost-efficiency, and extended clip lengths for AI models. This update aims to improve developer tools and effectiveness in AI applications.

ai.summary: Anthropic's AI R&D capabilities accelerated significantly, improving model performance on well-defined tasks at roughly twice the rate compared to 2024-2025. This acceleration primarily results from AI's increasing role in R&D, though multiple factors contributed in late 2025.

ai.title: Cloudflare's Trust Framework for AI Agents
ai.summary: Cloudflare has outlined the challenges websites face as AI agents increasingly act on behalf of users, making it harder to verify identities, assess trustworthiness, and assign accountability.

ai.summary: Blood on the Clocktower is a social deception game. Watching AI play the game unveils a lot about how AI is progressing on a set of AI capabilities that no other benchmark gives clear visibility into. The game requires AI to execute schemes with creativity, on-the-spot bluffing, and collective reasoning. This post looks at what happens when you pit AI models against each other in the game.

ai.summary: NVIDIA VFlash is a vision model that generates geometric predictions like robot trajectories and 3D motion in parallel rather than token by token.

ai.summary: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 platform now offers four open-weight models for interactive world simulation and driving scenes, each with 16 billion trainable parameters. These models enable multi-sensor data generation, synchronized observations, and photorealistic video from simulator controls, supporting advanced research in robotics and autonomous driving.

ai.summary: GPU providers sell capacity through reservations, on-demand rentals, and interruptible spot contracts. Reservations help secure financing through predictable revenue, on-demand offers flexibility at higher rates, and spot monetizes idle capacity. Ornn's compute price indices track executed on-demand transactions, excluding reservations and spot rentals.

webdev.title: Frontier Quality at 1% of the Cost: A Production Benchmark of LLM Classifiers
webdev.summary: Airbnb fine-tuned a model with 2 billion effective parameters to match frontier models on a production policy classifier, reaching 0.902 F1 with 35 ms median latency. At thousands of requests per minute, serving it on one GPU cost roughly 1% as much as frontier APIs, though hosted models were cheaper at low traffic.

webdev.title: React.lazy, Suspense and the Hidden 300 ms Delay
webdev.summary: Tab Widgets traced slow startup to React's 300 ms Suspense reveal throttle, even though its widget code had loaded within about 100 ms. Rendering placeholders without suspending brought the first widget content onscreen about 240 ms sooner in its Windows Chrome tests, while shrinking the startup bundle made no measurable difference.

webdev.title: Inside GitHub's New Git Storage Architecture
webdev.summary: GitHub's Rubicon architecture separates immutable Git objects in Azure Blob Storage from reference updates in a dedicated replicated log, letting compute, storage, and maintenance scale independently. Internal tests supported 5,000 concurrent agents and 7,200 pushes per second to one repository, with disposable virtual replicas serving requests and separate workers compacting packs.

webdev.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default
webdev.summary: Tests of ten design systems show why interaction performance needs the same attention as accessibility, using a 249-country dropdown and a list of 100 checkboxes as realistic stress cases. The practical approach combines Playwright performance budgets, checks for long frames and nonlinear scaling, and defaults such as automatic virtualization so every app benefits.

webdev.title: Don't Build the Reusable Component Yet
webdev.summary: Similar-looking workflows can have different failure modes, audit requirements, and owners, so combining them too early creates flags and coordination costs. Wait until a pattern appears three times for the same reason before extracting it, while sharing stable primitives, design tokens, accessibility behavior, and standards-driven utilities from the start.

webdev.title: Agents in Production. Free Dev Conference, Nov 12
webdev.summary: Do your agents need a boost? Explore agent memory, context engineering, MCP, evals, and multi-agent systems at Neo4j NODES 2026. Join developers for 100+ live technical sessions and an Andrew Ng keynote at this 24-hour online conference. Register free.

webdev.title: File Viewer
webdev.summary: File Viewer previews more than 275 file formats in the browser, including Office documents, PDF, CAD, 3D files, and archives. Its built-in renderers work without a conversion server, with integrations for Vue, React, Svelte, and Web Components and support for self-hosting workers, WASM, and fonts.

webdev.title: sidebearing-trim
webdev.summary: sidebearing-trim aligns text columns by visible letter shapes rather than glyph box origins. It reads OpenType glyph metrics and applies a negative offset at the start of the line to compensate for the first glyph's sidebearing.

webdev.title: GG Coder
webdev.summary: GG Coder is a desktop coding agent that works with existing AI subscriptions, API keys, or local models, with local search of open-source code and an autopilot that continues through verification. The repository also exposes reusable packages for provider connections, tool-using agents, model selection, and coding sessions under an AGPL-3.0 license.

webdev.title: A WebGPU Cat Puzzle Game Shipped in Three Days on Expo, with an AI Agent as the QA Team
webdev.summary: Purrkour went from first commit to App Store-ready in three days using a shared TypeScript engine, Expo, and TypeGPU, with procedural graphics and audio. A solver verifies the puzzles, while an AI agent tests actual gameplay through Argent using a debug bridge that exposes board state and exact tap coordinates.

webdev.title: How NVIDIA Uses AI Agents to Streamline AI Factory Operations
webdev.summary: NVIDIA uses specialized agents to correlate failures across GPU cluster hardware, networking, scheduling, and observability through one chat interface. The system can run on-premises with local Nemotron models, while read-only Kubernetes credentials, per-session sandboxes, and auditable recommendations give SREs control over investigations.

webdev.title: Discord Is Ditching Electron and Its New App Uses Less RAM
webdev.summary: Discord plans to replace Electron on desktop and React Native on mobile with shared Rust app code, while retaining native mobile interfaces. A preview Windows client used 290 MB of RAM, but there is no announced release date and user testing is still planned.

webdev.title: How a Split Webfont Slowed Down My Text Layout, and How I Fixed It
webdev.summary: Splitting common letters across webfont files increases text layout work and interaction latency, which can be reduced by keeping basic Latin together, avoiding overlapping unicode-range declarations, and placing Arabic fonts first on Arabic pages.

webdev.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small
webdev.summary: Thinking Machines' new mixture-of-experts model has 594B total parameters and 17B active, supports image input and adjustable reasoning effort, and launches on Tinker with Apache 2.0 weights planned for next week after external safety testing.

webdev.title: *sshole
webdev.summary: A password authentication bypass in OpenSSH on musl systems without PAM can let specially configured accounts accept long passwords because musl's crypt() failure marker matches the account's stored password field.

webdev.title: I Wish Tech Companies Knew More About Me
webdev.summary: Despite extensive tracking, tech services still recommend products people already own, ignore explicit language preferences, and miss years of consistent behavior, raising the question of why collected data so rarely improves the experience.

infosec.title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
infosec.summary: Attackers likely linked to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service used watering holes, proxy domains, and a compromised Ukrainian analytics service to inject JavaScript into mobile traffic. The code profiled visitors and delivered zero-click exploit chains against outdated iOS or Android devices, including DarkSword. Payloads sought browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and full device data. Targets included sites connected to US and UK diplomatic circles and Ukraine.

infosec.title: Chainalysis Warns All Users Hit In Cyber Breach Involving “Agentic” Techniques
infosec.summary: Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis released a warning that all of its users' data may have been compromised following an attack by a threat actor utilizing “offensive agentic techniques.” The stolen data includes names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens for all Chainalysis users. Chainalysis also temporarily took some other services offline, including its Know Your Transaction (KYT) cryptocurrency transaction monitoring service.

infosec.title: Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
infosec.summary: A browser extension with access to claude.ai can use Claude Dispatch to send prompts to Claude Desktop and achieve remote code execution. The attack exploits shared web and desktop sessions, repeated approval clicks, and a malicious npm package. It can also reach a work computer from a personal browser session. Anthropic knew of the issue in May but has not issued a fix. Dispatch remains available to existing users.

infosec.title: GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app
infosec.summary: An APK entry using a nonstandard compression method slips past libziparchive's size check, while libandroidfw memory-maps it at its full declared size. As a result, any process that reads a malformed resource receives a SIGBUS. That flaw lets an app with no code or permissions trap system_server in a boot loop that only a factory reset clears, or cause its own icon to crash on every uninstall screen. Bitdefender found it when a packed banking dropper in the wild crashed its emulators, but the persistent boot loop was its own escalation. Google declined to ship a security fix even though the bug reproduces on Android 10 through 17. With no patch coming, defenders should flag APKs whose ZIP entries use compression methods other than stored or deflate before they're installed, since an on-device warning may come too late.

infosec.title: Escaping Firecracker from Guest Userspace
infosec.summary: Coinspect demonstrated a Firecracker sandbox escape from guest userspace. CVE-2026-122192 allowed a guest to read and modify live Firecracker VMM memory and gain code execution in the host-side process. The flaw stemmed from a failed memory replacement after a snapshot-backed RAM discard, leaving a stale KVM memory slot pointing to reused VMM memory. A second issue, FC-03, allowed VMM code to use io_uring to perform host operations blocked by seccomp, including sending a network message to a host listener. Firecracker v0.23.0 through v1.16.1 are affected. v1.16.2 and v1.17.0 fix the escape.

infosec.title: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603
infosec.summary: Storm-2603 used the ONYPHE scanner to check a SharePoint server for ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770), waited three days, and on Christmas Eve loaded a webshell directly into IIS's w3wp.exe process memory. The webshell activated only for a specific User-Agent, tunneled into the internal network with suo5, escalated to SYSTEM using EfsPotato, and then moved to a vulnerable Velociraptor build, an EDR-killer driver, and a blocked Warlock ransomware attempt. Kaspersky attributed the intrusion with moderate confidence. Defenders should hunt for IIS paths that resolve in config but have no file on disk, which appear as IIS-Configuration ETW events 25 and 47 without the usual file-change monitoring events. Kaspersky has released CLRDeserializationExploitFinder to flag the deserialization exploit itself.

infosec.title: Forrester study: securing the data your agents can reach reduces breach exposure risk by 65%
infosec.summary: Rather than trying to inspect every agent request as it happens, the world's top enterprises are using Sentra to govern the data that agents can access. And it's paying off: the Forrester Total Economic Impact™ Study for Sentra found that agentic data security generates 351% ROI with 65% reduced breach exposure risk. Read the report

infosec.title: synology-nas-cli
infosec.summary: synology-nas-cli checks a Synology NAS for the exposures exploited in October's C3RB3R/.L0CK3D ransomware campaign: unpatched DSM builds, vulnerable SA-26:14 packages, QuickConnect and UPnP port forwarding, SMB1, ransom notes, and CVE-2024-10441 exploit traces. It shows each fix as a before-and-after dry-run plan, applies it, and reads every setting back to confirm. If encryption is already running, it can freeze the encryptor with SIGSTOP and capture its memory to recover keys. It's a zero-dependency Python CLI with an MCP server, so a Claude Code or Codex agent can run the audit end to end.

infosec.title: Sectiv
infosec.summary: Sectiv is a Burp Suite extension that runs captured proxy traffic past an LLM, guided by editable "skills" for IDOR, XSS, SQLi, and SSRF, and returns triaged findings with CVSS scores and HTML, Python, or curl PoCs. Testers can load two accounts to help the model reason about broken access control. It masks cookies, tokens, and JWTs before sending traffic to providers like OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama model. Skills can be imported, exported, and tailored per target, and findings export to HTML, Markdown, or JSON for reporting.

infosec.title: GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
infosec.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber built working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, more than five times GPT-5.6 Sol's count with the same harness, and found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox bugs. OpenAI also trained it to stay within the scope a researcher sets: on a honeypot evaluation, it avoided easy-to-exploit, out-of-scope services in 99.93% of runs without a safety prompt and 100% with one, enough for OpenAI to rate it Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework. Approved defenders reach it through Daybreak Red, which requires IP allowlisting by default and runs misuse monitoring, and a new tier gives critical infrastructure teams authorized OT/ICS testing.

infosec.title: Apple Will Scan Shared iCloud Links for Harmful Content, but Won't Explain What Counts as Harmful
infosec.summary: Apple will check photos and files shared via iCloud's “Anyone with the Link” setting for harmful content on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27.3. Publicly shared items lose end-to-end encryption, even with Advanced Data Protection enabled. Apple can remove files, block accounts, prevent re-registration, and contact law enforcement. It has not defined “harmful,” explained the screening method, said whether people review flags, or confirmed whether existing public links are covered.

infosec.title: OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run
infosec.summary: OpenAI says an automated pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities in 30 hours and generated 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits. The run produced 291 information-leak proofs of concept, patches for identified flaws, and at least 10 novel exploitation techniques. It cost $1.21 million in API credits, or $1,279 per exploit. OpenAI says unpatched systems with low-privileged access should be treated as accessible to well-resourced attackers with root access.

infosec.title: Bank Phishing Sites Show Fake ‘Suspended' Pages to Evade Takedowns
infosec.summary: Kela found more than 300 fake bank domains using a phishing kit that records visitor IP addresses. First visits receive bank login pages. Repeat visits receive a fake hosting "suspended" notice. This can make takedown teams classify live sites as inactive. The campaign targets business banking and treasury logins at 189 US institutions, with activity also seen in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand.

infosec.title: Cyberattack on Norway's aid agency may have swept up all user data
infosec.summary: Attackers used 27 compromised accounts to enter Norad's Grants Portal, potentially exposing names and email addresses for all 20,614 registered users, and also took applications and documents from three foreign organizations.

infosec.title: Chinese Nation-State Threat Activity Falls Sharply in Q2 and Q3 2026
infosec.summary: Trellix detected 41.4% less China-aligned nation-state activity from April to September, but cautioned that the drop may reflect shifts in targeting or its own visibility rather than less hacking, since PRC activity still outpaced Russia and Iran, while the US and Turkey together drew three-quarters of all nation-state detections.

infosec.title: AWS Security Hub now provides an SBOM inventory for your compute resources
infosec.summary: AWS Security Hub now shows an organization-wide inventory of the software packages installed across EC2 instances, ECR images, and Lambda functions, built from Amazon Inspector's SBOMs and queryable through the API, at no extra cost wherever Inspector is enabled.

devops.summary: Chainguard Actions is now Generally Available: a hardened catalog of over 1,000 popular actions, delivered as drop-in replacements for the actions developers already want to use. > Continuously verified and hardened as upstream versions ship and attack patterns emerge. >Every action includes a HARDENING.md report detailing which vulnerabilities were found and removed. >One-business-day SLA for new action requests. devops.title: Alpine Linux Security Advisory: OpenSSH-server password authentication bypass
devops.summary: A vulnerability in Alpine Linux's openssh-server package allows attackers to bypass password authentication and log in without knowing any password. The flaw affects releases 3.16 through 3.24 and allows remote access if the system has an account with no password set. Users should update openssh and restart sshd or disable password logins immediately.

devops.title: Powering open infrastructure for autonomous agents
devops.summary: Google donated Agent Substrate, gVisor, and OpenRL to the CNCF Sandbox and announced the general availability of Agent Substrate on GKE. Agent Substrate decouples stateful agent sessions from compute to restore idle sessions in under 500 milliseconds. The project achieves 10x standard container density and performs over 500 suspend and resume activations per second.

devops.title: Running Production With Zero Stored Logs
devops.summary: This post describes how to run a K3s platform of more than 15 microservices with no centralized log collection, relying on filtered Prometheus metrics and temporary verbose logging. It notes trade-offs, including the need to anticipate questions and unsuitability for audits requiring immutable trails.

devops.title: When the Kubernetes API went silent: A three-layer networking mystery
devops.summary: Google traced intermittent GKE API timeouts to three interacting failures: Private Service Connect reordered packets, Envoy kept half-closed sockets open, and a Linux TCP bug prevented those sockets from closing. Simultaneous packet captures at multiple points exposed the reordering, and a Linux kernel patch fixed the underlying TCP bug.

devops.title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
devops.summary: Docker identifies five risks of autonomous AI agents, including prompt injection, credential exposure, and data exfiltration. It recommends isolation and governance through Docker Sandboxes and AI Governance rather than model improvements alone.

devops.title: The Google SRE Book was written before AI started writing the code.
devops.summary: Systems now change faster than teams can track, and AI features can look healthy while giving wrong answers. The AI SRE Handbook covers what that means for reliability, how to evaluate an AI SRE, and benchmark results from 25 real Sev1-3 incidents. Download the handbook .

devops.title: agent-browser
devops.summary: agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives AI agents a browser they can drive one shell command at a time. It reads pages as a compact accessibility tree and allows agents to interact with elements through refs. The tool supports Chrome for Testing, Mobile Safari, and various cloud browser providers.

devops.title: Auto Ontology
devops.summary: NVIDIA Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over enterprise data. The open source library builds context layers from metadata to enable deterministic query generation and more explainable AI for LLM workflows. It exposes this context to agents via MCP, CLI, and API access.

devops.title: What Is the OpenTofu MCP Server and How to Use It
devops.summary: Spacelift explains the official OpenTofu MCP server, which offers seven read-only tools for searching registry documentation for providers, modules, resources, and data sources. It runs from a hosted endpoint or locally with npx and never runs tofu commands or reads state.

devops.title: Trace linkage: connect the dots between your app traces and database queries
devops.summary: Grafana Cloud made trace linkage generally available in Database Observability. It connects OpenTelemetry application traces to database query data collected by Alloy, matching by query.

devops.title: Reliability in the AI Era: AI That Works the Incident With You
devops.summary: PagerDuty announced the PD Reliability Platform and PD Labs alongside its Paige SRE agent.

devops.title: Evaluate your AI agents with Fireworks AI models in Datadog Agent Observability
devops.summary: Datadog Agent Observability now supports Fireworks AI as a model provider.

devops.title: Announcing the OpenTelemetry JavaScript SDK 3.0
devops.summary: OpenTelemetry JavaScript SDK 3.0 introduces ESM-only support and removes compatibility with older Node.js versions.

Tested on 10 hours of real Wispr Flow dictations from more than 2,300 speakers, Canto had the lowest word error rate of every model tested from the major AI labs. product.title: The end of feature discovery as we know it
product.summary: AI agents will eliminate traditional software feature discovery by operating products on users' behalf. Instead of navigating menus, users can invoke functionality directly using natural language, forcing product teams to focus on trust and minimal AI interfaces.

product.title: Voice of the Customer
product.summary: Effective product building requires mastering the Voice of the Customer to understand underlying needs rather than surface-level metrics. AI accelerates this process, turning research loops into quick conversations and creating accessible organizational knowledge bases.

product.title: The Bottleneck Has Moved
product.summary: With AI agents coding rapidly, the main constraint in software development has shifted away from writing code. Enterprises must reorganize around end-to-end value delivery, measuring time-to-learn rather than raw velocity.

product.title: The harness is a product
product.summary: As agentic AI systems evolve, the underlying harness (instructions, tools, and sandboxes) must be managed as a discrete product. Product teams must apply rigorous testing and proper rollback paths to ensure reliability and prevent configuration debt.

product.summary: Ramp co-CEO Eric Glyman shares insights on product strategy, hiring based on proof of work, and building tools internally first. The startup maintains small, autonomous teams to stay nimble as it scales.

product.title: Activation metric or motivation detector?
product.summary: This article outlines a method for validating activation metrics, ensuring they drive downstream retention rather than just detecting pre-existing motivation. Teams must separate genuine aha moments from survivorship bias to fix drop-off root causes.

product.title: There's a 60% Chance of Rain
product.summary: Teams can use Monte Carlo simulations on historical throughput data to generate probabilistic delivery forecasts. Teams can better navigate uncertainty and risk by analyzing past weekly output instead of single fixed dates.

product.title: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the AI
product.summary: In an era of cheap AI generation, product managers must move past preventing low-quality software. Instead, they should focus on directing product strategy, standardizing patterns, and practicing detached engagement with outcomes.

product.title: If X, then Y

design.title: YouTube is giving its Android navigation bar a Liquid Glass-y makeover
design.summary: Google is testing a translucent floating bottom navigation bar in YouTube for Android, replacing the conventional attached navigation area with a design resembling Apple's Liquid Glass aesthetic. The experiment follows other recent navigation changes, including a separate test that removes the Subscriptions tab, and has prompted criticism that Google is borrowing from Apple's design language instead of following Material 3 Expressive. The new appearance appears to be controlled through a limited server-side experiment, with no official way to enable it manually.

design.title: ChatGPT can now turn your images into GIFs with its latest update
design.summary: OpenAI's Images 2.6 update introduces GIF generation across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, allowing static illustrations, characters, and product visuals to become short looping animations. Image generation is now up to 50% faster, with improved consistency across edits and two new API models: Flare for speed and Sunburst for higher-quality detail. Developers also gain image markup for targeted edits, SVG export, and controls for how much planning the model performs before generating an image.

design.title: Pangram, the Gold Standard for AI Text Checks, Releases Image 1.0 Tool to Sniff Fake Pics and Videos
design.summary: Pangram says Image 1.0 detected AI-generated pictures with 99.96% accuracy on its own evaluation set. The detector is available on the web, via API, and as a Chrome extension. Video detection runs on a lighter frame-by-frame model that scores 98.7% on the DF26 benchmark, ahead of TruthScan and Sightengine. Heatmaps show which parts of an image are AI-generated, and images as small as 256×256 pixels can be checked, with lower confidence below 512×512.

design.title: AI can generate the interface. What makes it worth caring about?
design.summary: AI can generate polished, consistent interfaces, but deciding when an experience should feel playful, surprising, celebratory, or restrained requires understanding the people and situations involved. A confetti animation might be appropriate after someone completes a major personal milestone but distracting when an administrator finishes a routine task for the forty-seventh time. Expressive design should therefore be evaluated for its purpose, context, accessibility, and potential to interrupt users rather than treated as decoration that makes every interaction more engaging.

design.title: How Figma Manages Sandboxes at Scale
design.summary: Figma's AI products, including its agent and Figma Make, need tens of thousands of sandboxes to run untrusted code safely. Nimbus, an internal platform, provisions, monitors, and routes those sandboxes across cloud providers through one simple API. Warm pools of pre-started sandboxes cut provisioning latency by about 90% and, together with automated provider selection, lifted provisioning availability from 99% to 99.95%.

design.title: Fortune Telling and Speculative Design
design.summary: Design engineers are particularly well positioned to explore possible futures because they combine visual design, software development, and the ability to build convincing working prototypes. Maggie Appleton's approach at GitHub Next involves collecting weak signals of emerging change, developing theories about where technology is heading, and creating tangible artifacts that make those possibilities easier to evaluate. Rather than trying to predict one inevitable future, speculative design helps teams investigate multiple plausible directions and make better decisions about what to build next.

design.title: Headless Web Components
design.summary: Slab handles the hard parts of a component — keyboard and focus, ARIA, forms, and events — on top of the native elements browsers already ship.

design.title: Advanced Typography with CSS
design.summary: CSS Type Studio lets you quickly iterate through different typefaces, sizes, spacing attributes, and more.

design.title: Animated Components for React and React Native
design.summary: Copy-paste components for React and Next.js, built with Motion and Tailwind CSS. Free, open source, and fully customizable.

design.title: Win the Demo, Lose the Market: Why Breakthrough Technology Isn't Enough
design.summary: Proterra delivered over 1,000 electric buses and grew revenue 24% in 2022, then filed for Chapter 11 the following year. Its buses worked, but below-cost pricing and order-by-order customization undid the business, because technical superiority is not the same as competitive advantage. Five shifts, from listing capabilities to defining consequences and from claims to proof, turn product advantage into enterprise advantage.

design.title: Tatiana Egoshina finds beauty in bad typography, Italian folklore and happy accidents
design.summary: Milan-based designer Tatiana Egoshina draws inspiration from unexpected everyday details, imperfect typography, and Italian folklore, transforming local stories and accidental discoveries into colorful identities, illustrations, and installations, including an award-winning projection onto the cliffs of southern Italy.

design.title: Major design IP reforms announced to tackle copycats, courtroom costs, and SUD protection
design.summary: The UK government has announced major reforms to design intellectual property protections aimed at making registration and enforcement fairer and more affordable for independent designers and small studios. Proposed changes would give the Intellectual Property Office stronger powers to reject copied or bad-faith registrations, addressing practices in which competitors register someone else's designs and use them to force legitimate products off online marketplaces. Registered design disputes would also become eligible for the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court's Small Claims Track, allowing creators to pursue claims of up to £10,000 without facing the substantial legal costs of conventional litigation.

design.title: These Classic Design Fails are Still Making Us Laugh
design.summary: Classic design fails, from Tesco's buttermilk carton to a UK government logo that looks rude when rotated 90 degrees, still raise plenty of laughs.

design.title: Actor Johnny Depp Showcases His Artistic Side with Painting Exhibition in London
design.summary: Halcyon Gallery in London hosts Johnny Depp's first major UK exhibition of original works, running from October 13 to November 15.

marketing.title: Holiday marketing is a timing game
marketing.summary: From holiday promotions and customer appreciation to New Year campaigns, timing can make all the difference. Lob's Holiday Direct Mail Kit helps marketers plan seasonal campaigns with a campaign calendar, customizable mail templates, and practical guidance on when to send. Explore examples for retail, healthcare, financial services, and real estate, plus tips for personalization, targeting, and coordinating direct mail with email, social, and digital ads. Explore the Holiday Direct Mail Kit to take the guesswork out of your next seasonal campaign.

marketing.title: More Than Half of Marketers Have No Clear Read on UGC Creator ROI
marketing.summary: 57% of marketers have no clear understanding of whether UGC creator spending delivers positive returns, with 38% not measuring creator costs against acquisition economics. Nearly half of teams allocate less than 5% of ad spend to UGC. Instagram and TikTok are the top creator sourcing channels at 74%. Authenticity is the top creator selection criterion, with 96% prioritizing creators who are authentic on camera.

marketing.title: Is Something Up With YouTube's Ad Business?
marketing.summary: YouTube's ad revenue growth is slowing despite its growing share of TV viewing, raising questions about whether it can convert its CTV audience into more advertising dollars. Its ad revenue grew 9% to $11.2 billion in Q3, even as it captured 15.8% of total TV viewing. Several factors may explain the gap: YouTube missed out on political ad spending, some brands still view FAST platforms as more traditional TV environments, and advertisers are diversifying their CTV budgets instead of concentrating spend on YouTube. Growing competition from Meta and YouTube's expanding ad-free subscription options may also limit its advertising growth.

marketing.title: Why AI influencers work better with a human friend
marketing.summary: Seeing an AI influencer relate to a real person makes it seem more human, which raises trust and lifts engagement. Posts showing them sharing a genuine moment with a real person, like eating together or posing arm in arm, drew about 21% more engagement in a sample of 10,000 IG posts. A bystander in the frame or a second AI character has no effect, and the lift is biggest for the most artificial-looking avatars.

marketing.title: Win Report: How an infographic increased conversions by 15%
marketing.summary: DiamondBack Covers increased product page conversions by 15% by replacing an early product gallery image with an infographic that paired key product features with their customer benefits. Research found that 43% of buyers cited security as their main purchase reason, yet fewer than 13% of visitors scrolled far enough to see important selling messages about protection and durability. The infographic highlighted four selling points: durable aluminum construction, gas spring-assisted openings, weatherproof seals, and secure locking mechanisms. Pairing each feature with a specific benefit gave shoppers both a reason to care and proof to support the claim.

marketing.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR

marketing.title: Find Site Errors with AI Before Ads Run
marketing.summary: Use AI to audit campaign landing pages before ads go live and catch problems that could prevent shoppers from converting. Tools like ChatGPT and Claude can review screenshots, page content, and crawl reports to identify broken links, conflicting offers, inaccurate product availability, missing information, and mobile layout issues. Pair AI analysis with technical tools like Google Lighthouse and Screaming Frog, then manually test the shopping journey on desktop and mobile, including checkout and ad conversion tracking. Prioritize issues by their potential impact on customers, and repeat the audit before every campaign.

marketing.title: Reddit 2027 Moments Annual Guide
marketing.summary: This Reddit guide maps cultural events, sports, and life milestones that brands can use to plan campaigns around community conversations. 3 in 4 Reddit users are open to considering a new brand after seeing a community recommendation, even if it costs more. Half of shoppers use Reddit to verify AI recommendations, while 56% of holiday shoppers look for deals and promotions before buying.

marketing.title: Reddit just stopped giving itself away
marketing.summary: Reddit is testing a logged-in-only experience to reduce unmonetized traffic and protect its content from AI scraping. The move follows a 53% revenue increase but slower user growth in the US. Meanwhile, Discord is making public communities searchable on Google to attract new members. Both platforms are adapting to AI-driven search by balancing public content discovery with member access.

marketing.title: Narrative Intelligence vs. Social Listening: What's the Difference?
marketing.summary: Social listening measures what people discuss online through metrics like mentions, reach, and sentiment. Narrative Intelligence adds context by revealing how topics are interpreted through different narratives. It identifies who is shaping conversations and which communities are driving or encountering them. The two approaches work together to help teams understand why conversations matter. For example, overall sentiment may appear neutral while a specific narrative contains concentrated negative sentiment.

marketing.title: We pushed acquisition too hard. Complaints followed
marketing.summary: After increasing co-registration subscribers for its Trivia Nut newsletter, a publisher saw Gmail's spam complaint rate exceed 0.30% for 4 days and peak at 0.49%. It cut incoming subscriber volume by 50%, bringing the next reported rate down to 0.06%. The publisher recommends monitoring Gmail's spam rate separately through Postmaster Tools and checking acquisition sources when complaints rise.

marketing.title: Only 54% of Consumers Trust That Black Friday Discounts Are Lower Than Normal
marketing.summary: Retailer reputation and money-back guarantees build the most trust in a deal, while influencer recommendations rank last.

marketing.summary: Character-led campaigns are more likely to report big market share gains, 41% versus 30%, yet brands largely dropped mascots until AI companies revived them.

founders.title: Growth is becoming an engineering problem
founders.summary: The most AI-pilled teams are rebilling their entire GTM stacks. Small and medium businesses are actively trying to use agents to recreate software as some of their old tools aren't making the cut. Larger companies have contracts, integrations, and years of operational habits to work through. This post looks at the growth teams rebuilding their GTM stacks around agents to see what they're building, buying, or replacing.

founders.title: The end of feature discovery as we know it
founders.summary: Growth teams used to spend months getting customers to try a feature they'd just shipped. Lovable's growth lead now flags it in Slack when the agent itself doesn't know about a feature, because customers describe a job and leave it to the agent to pick the tools. The next sign of adoption is a customer handing the agent a whole workflow after trusting it with a small task. That customer might spend less time in the app, so the product has to show what the agent decided and give them a way to undo it.

founders.title: Find high-value members with a Claude agent
founders.summary: Selling to wealthy consumers can look a lot like selling enterprise software. Atlas' founder says the typical member spends about $1 million a year on cards, so he started treating members like key accounts. He used a Claude agent to find existing members the company could do more for and called them himself. A few of those conversations ended with six-figure trips booked through the company's concierge.

founders.title: Startup marketing advice in the age of AI
founders.summary: AI can turn out a finished launch video before anyone has checked whether it could pass for a competitor's. One startup marketer recommends covering your name and logo with a competitor's and watching or reading the whole thing through. Start with a rushed tagline or the stock footage between demos. Rewrite anything the competitor could still use as is, and keep the lines and shots that stop making sense under their logo.

founders.title: Agentic banking is here to stay. Here's how Mercury keeps you in control
founders.summary: Mercury lets AI agents prepare payments or transfers that a person still has to approve under the team's existing rules. The agent can only use permissions its owner already has, so an employee who can't see the payroll balance can't get it through an agent either. Admins can review each agent's activity and see who connected it. They can also revoke access from Mercury on the web.

founders.title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
founders.summary: Vercel Schedules allows agents and applications to create, change, or cancel one-time and recurring schedules through code without redeploying. They are designed to let users and agents decide when work should happen while applications are still running. A schedule tells Vercel when to trigger a task and where to send it. Applications provide the code that carries out the work. Schedules can be used for both static and dynamic jobs.

founders.title: Now available: Retention messages for subscriptions
founders.summary: Apple's Retention Messaging API is a server-to-server service that enables developers to select messages to display to customers when they view a subscription details page and might cancel. Retention messages can include text, images, or a special offer. The API allows developers to choose which message to show subscribers based on their subscription details. API access is available by request.

founders.title: AX is not the new DX, it's the new UX
founders.summary: The Agent Experience has become one of the most talked-about shifts in infrastructure over the past year. The focus has been on rebuilding developer tools for coding agents, but that's just because coding agents got good first. Every product is becoming something agents use. As time goes on, more and more users will be agents.

founders.title: Is Private Equity Cooked?
founders.summary: Private equity firms could borrow to buy mature software companies because lenders could count on their customers renewing. AI is making those renewals harder to bank on, just as higher rates make the next buyout harder to finance. It is estimated that a typical buyout now needs 10% to 12% annual EBITDA growth to match what a 2015 deal could earn with about 5%. That's a higher bar for the next buyer at a time when revenue growth at Golub Capital's software borrowers has slowed from 9% to under 3% in two years.

crypto.title: Circle Q3 2026: $865M Revenue, 85% EBITDA Beat, Binance $100M Investment
crypto.summary: Circle reported Q3 2026 revenue of $864.9M and adjusted EBITDA of $317M, beating consensus by 85% as USDC minting reached $104B against an $82.45B estimate. Binance committed a $100M equity investment and expanded its USDC partnership, while Circle agreed to acquire Tazapay to add $25B+ in annualized payment volume across 100+ markets. Samsung Wallet and Visa Direct deployments extended USDC access to bank accounts in 60+ countries and payout rails across 180+ countries. USDC market share slipped 1.83 percentage points year-over-year to 27%, and Circle cut ~5% of staff as reserve income (about 75% of revenue) faces pressure from falling rates.

crypto.title: Democratic sweep of Congress forces crypto industry to rethink strategy
crypto.summary: Democrats took both chambers, and Stand With Crypto counts 19 pro-crypto senators and 226 House members elected against 8 and 106 anti-crypto. Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted in Ohio despite more than $60M in crypto PAC spending against him. TD Cowen says the Clarity Act is unlikely to advance for two years and expects investigations into World Liberty Financial. Fairshake spent $154.5M this cycle, and one industry source said the money would have been better spent on direct lobbying. Industry voices stress that crypto is bipartisan, and focus is expected to shift to taxes and security after the Binance hack.

crypto.title: Power Perps on Hyperliquid
crypto.summary: Paragon introduced Power Perps on Hyperliquid, a family of perpetual contracts that track an asset's price raised to a power, with HYPE² as the first instrument delivering 4x exposure when the underlying doubles. The structure carries no strikes or expiry dates, consolidating trader interest into a single persistent order book per underlying rather than fragmenting liquidity across an options chain as conventional instruments do. Hyperliquid's portfolio margin allows cross-margining of spot, linear perps, and Power Perps in one account, while market makers hedging delta in existing spot and perp books add order flow that tightens Power Perp spreads. Paragon frames these contracts as composable building blocks: a squared perp paired with a short linear approximates a straddle, while the reverse combination, short power and long linear, earns funding when the market trades sideways.

crypto.title: Blast L2 Shuts Down, Opens 12-Month Asset Recovery Window
crypto.summary: Blast L2, launched in early 2024 with native yield on deposited ETH and stablecoins and peak TVL in the billions, has shut down. Users with assets in L2 wallets, pending withdrawals, or Blast Mobile can recover ETH and USD via the team's recovery site through November 4, 2027. Unclaimed funds after that date may be unrecoverable. The closure ends one of 2024's prominent yield-bearing L2 experiments, where protocol-level auto-yield on deposits served as the primary TVL acquisition mechanism rather than external incentive programs.

crypto.title: Payments Are the New Ads
crypto.summary: Agentic commerce has exposed a structural gap in payments: AI shopping agents have four paths to pay, each with material friction, and broken flows have deterred 60% of UK adults from trusting agent purchases after a single failure. Stripe's Instinct Balance, a prefunded stablecoin wallet, sidesteps bank authentication friction and earns Stripe ~$1.95 per $100 spent compared to ~$0.40 on virtual cards, a 4x unit-economics advantage over the network-token path. Banks have a counter through agent-authenticated network tokens modeled on Apple Pay's 2014 liability deal, but Chase has not joined any major agent platform, leaving the token infrastructure incomplete. If stablecoin balances capture agentic spend before banks resolve token liability, those funds exit bank deposits for good, shifting the customer-ownership fight from card rails to stablecoin custodians.

crypto.title: Reusable Networks: Why AI Makes Crypto's Network Effects Valuable
crypto.summary: As AI drives software production costs toward zero, value migrates from applications to the networks they compose with: protocol liquidity, on-chain identity graphs, reputation systems, and settlement rails. AI can clone interfaces and regenerate code in minutes, but it cannot reproduce the provenance of an NFT, the liquidity depth of Uniswap, or the trust accumulated in USDC. This reframes crypto's composability thesis: when any application becomes a commodity, the scarce asset is access to the shared state layer underneath. Blockchains were designed as canonical internet-layer state, and in a world where agents need reliable, permissionless coordination infrastructure, that original premise becomes a stronger value proposition.

crypto.title: No One Needs Blockchain
crypto.summary: The CFTC's approval of single-stock perpetual futures, matched by Kalshi's same-day launch, illustrates a structural trend: 2026's crypto growth concentrated in businesses treating blockchain as financial rails, while onchain-native DeFi lagged. Kalshi's architecture is representative, with orders matched in a proprietary engine and clearing running through a registered DCO, leaving blockchain to handle only stablecoin deposits/withdrawals and tokenized positions on Solana. The two growth clusters, speculation-driven (prediction markets, perps, and memecoins) and TradFi-connected (stablecoins, RWAs, and vaults), share the same pattern: platforms owning user relationships capture revenue, and blockchain captures infrastructure fees. This creates a value capture problem for the ecosystem, which risks commoditization unless more businesses emerge where blockchain is indispensable to core logic rather than settlement infrastructure.

crypto.title: Why Stripe Will Lose Agentic Payments
crypto.summary: Stripe's two agentic payment methods, Shared Payment Tokens (zero merchant adoption and opposed by card networks) and issued virtual cards (single-auth limits, no rewards, and identity mismatches), both fail to satisfy networks and end users, while Shopify now carries Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Discover agent tokens natively through Shop Pay without routing credentials through Stripe. The structural argument is that the industry will skip Stripe's intermediary layer entirely, moving from raw PANs directly to native agent token standards like VIC and AgentPay, which makes Stripe's existing network effects irrelevant. Startups that build UX around native agent token flows rather than Stripe credentials are positioned to capture agentic commerce distribution as credential ownership shifts to the card networks themselves.

crypto.title: Arkansas sues Kalshi, alleging illegal gambling and mental health harms
crypto.summary: Arkansas AG Tim Griffin filed suit alleging Kalshi runs an illegal gambling platform, citing risks like excessive wagering, financial losses, and depression.

Microsoft keeps the platform running, but your organization remains responsible for protecting its data. Third-party backup can meet recovery needs that built-in tools may not cover. it.title: Apple reportedly cuts employee AI budgets
it.summary: Apple is reportedly reducing employee allowances for third-party AI tools, with proposed daily caps of $100 for engineers and $25 for other staff. Some teams are also being encouraged to use cheaper or locally hosted models, although Apple hasn't confirmed the changes.

it.title: Microsoft expands unpublished Copilot Chat limits
it.summary: Microsoft is expanding usage caps for commercial Copilot Chat users without a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license, but won't disclose the limits or let administrators adjust them. The rollout began November 2 for smaller organizations and reaches those with more than 2,000 seats November 9.

it.title: What's new across Google's Agentic Data Cloud
it.summary: Google Cloud has announced major updates to its Agentic Data Cloud, introducing features like a borderless Lakehouse powered by Apache Iceberg, enhanced Knowledge Catalog context curation, and specialized infrastructure for scaling AI agents. These capabilities aim to give agents secure, real-time access to distributed enterprise data while lowering token costs and improving query performance. The announcements also include new development kits and integrated Gemini tools designed to assist both data practitioners and business users.

it.title: AI just raised the interest rate on your technical debt
it.summary: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery effectively raises the interest rate on technical debt by making exploits much cheaper and faster to develop. While finding bugs has become vastly accelerated, repairing them still moves at human speed, creating a dangerous asymmetry for organizations. Leadership teams should look into auditing deferred security tickets, sunsetting unused internet-facing systems, and reviewing accepted-risk registers on a regular schedule.

it.title: Who Checks the Boring Layer
it.summary: While high-profile security incidents often involve complex exploits, the underlying entry points frequently rely on basic vulnerabilities like missing access controls, unpatched firmware, and exposed credentials. Coding tools and internal agents can exacerbate risks if the surrounding access layer and operational security are not strictly managed and reviewed.

it.title: Introducing MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027: one foundation for the agentic enterprise
it.summary: MariaDB has introduced its Enterprise Platform 2027, a unified data foundation designed for AI agents and enterprise workloads. The platform combines transactions, real-time analytics, vector search, and AI tooling such as Agent Memory and Semantic Cache to reduce latency and token costs. Additionally, it delivers a 56 percent increase in peak throughput compared to version 11.8 and introduces multi-region active-active scalability via MariaDB Raft Cluster.

it.title: Confluent brings live SQL queries to streaming data
it.summary: Confluent made Lightning Tables generally available on AWS, letting applications query continuously updated Kafka data through SQL and APIs without maintaining a separate serving database. The launch supports its Streamhouse architecture, which combines streaming, processing, governance, and querying to give applications and AI agents current business context.

it.title: How to Use Test-Driven Development with AI Agents (Without Lowering Code Quality)
it.summary: A new empirical workflow called EXACT combines Test-Driven Development with agentic AI tools while maintaining code quality. The approach utilizes example mapping for collaborative human modeling, natural language test lists, and predictive TDD. Experiments show that this method significantly improves correctness and code quality compared to unguided vibe coding or plain TDD prompts.

it.title: Google explains why its London backup generators failed
it.summary: Google's newly detailed postmortem attributes its October London outage to a voltage-sensing flaw and controller misconfiguration that prevented backup generators from starting. One power feed was already undergoing repairs when the other failed, leaving battery backups to run out before power could be restored.

it.title: Why the next generation of ERP is all about outcomes

it.title: Introducing AlloyDB Express for rapid testing and prototyping

hardware.title: Agility Robotics lists on Nasdaq as AGLT with $1.8M of revenue and a $138.1M net loss

In 2025, it booked $1.8 million of revenue, over half from five robots bought by one investor, against a $138.1 million net loss. About $38 million of that was non-cash stock compensation, and it burned $99.8 million in cash.

hardware.title: Waymo confirms it will leave Uber in Austin and Atlanta in January 2028
hardware.summary: Waymo will move rides in Austin and Atlanta to its own app in January 2028, ahead of the Uber deal's May 2028 expiry. Riders on Uber never knew whether they'd get a robotaxi or a human driver. Waymo wants a direct rider relationship.

hardware.title: Blue Origin adds a BE-7 third stage to New Glenn and unveils the Northstar engine
hardware.summary: Northstar is a methalox booster engine that Blue Origin says cuts mass by 30% and parts count by 50% versus the BE-4 while raising thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 lbf, with assembly in under a day. No first-flight date is given, and New Glenn is still recovering from a pad explosion that happened in May.

hardware.title: Qualcomm to supply MIMO radios and baseband for Starlink Mobile's terrestrial 5G network
hardware.summary: SpaceX has signed a multiyear deal for Qualcomm's Dragonwing infrastructure platforms: the QRU100 radio unit and QDU100 distributed unit, with 64T64R massive MIMO and physical-layer RAN software. They'll go into base stations at what's planned as tens of thousands of US sites, starting in 2027, to complement Starlink's satellite service. Qualcomm calls this its biggest 5G deal yet.

hardware.title: FLIP software subtracts starlight in JWST coronagraph data with up to 15x better sensitivity
hardware.summary: A Northwestern-led team built FLIP, which makes a physics-based digital twin of the telescope's optics and adjusts it until it reproduces the observed starlight, then subtracts that simulated glare. On existing NIRCam data at 4.3 microns, it improved sensitivity up to 15x over the conventional KLIP method and recovered the giant planet 51 Eridani b, which standard processing couldn't separate from residual glare.

hardware.title: LumiTac is a camera-free six-axis tactile sensor, 12 mm wide and about $7 in parts
hardware.summary: LumiTac pairs five photoemitters with five RGBW photoreceivers on opposing circuit boards joined by translucent silicone, so load-driven motion between the layers shifts the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The head is 12 mm across, 4.75 mm thick, under 2 g, and made with about $7 in components. Independent testing gave R² of 0.966 to 0.994, with mean absolute errors of 0.054 to 0.190 N in force and 0.304 to 1.419 mN·m in moment.

hardware.title: Texas governor-elect Hinojosa's data center moratorium pledge puts 13.3 GW of announced projects at risk
hardware.summary: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to halt all data center approvals until the legislature passes new laws when it meets in January. Outgoing Governor Abbott had already paused new grid connections and ordered an audit. Texas holds about 25% of planned US data center capacity. It is estimated that 13.3 GW of announced projects are at risk.

hardware.title: CXMT's chairman tops China's newcomers at $13B on an unverified claim of a 4F² DRAM breakthrough
hardware.summary: CXMT says its 4F² DRAM uses a vertical surrounding gate transistor and builds the memory cells and peripheral circuitry on separate wafers joined by hybrid bonding, which an analyst says could raise density by about 30%. Yields are unknown, and a server product is promised before year-end. The claim cut Samsung and SK Hynix about 13% in a day, even though CXMT holds roughly 10% of DRAM against Samsung's 38%.

hardware.title: Shield Space plans swarms of up to 100 laser-armed cubesat interceptors, starting with a 2027 rendezvous demo
hardware.summary: UK startup Shield Space wants carrier-deployed cubesat swarms using lasers, microwaves, or kinetic standoff to defend satellites, even when ground contact is lost, for under £100M per 100.

hardware.title: Starfish's first Otter servicing spacecraft is lost to a fault-protection fault, ending a $15M NASA inspection mission
hardware.summary: Starfish's Otter 24C launched October 1, made two-way contact, and downlinked telemetry, then lost contact during commissioning.

hardware.title: Thea Energy and MIT will test a full-size flat superconducting coil for the Eos stellarator
hardware.summary: Thea Energy's Eos stellarator uses flat coils instead of hard-to-build 3D magnets.

hardware.title: Walmart adds 300 Zipline drone delivery sites, building on 2M+ deliveries
hardware.summary: Walmart signed a multi-year deal to add 300 Zipline drone sites.
